messages.content: Put this into reported speech: Neha said, "I am going to the library because I need a book on volcanoes."
Neha said that she was going to the library because she needed a book on volcanoes.
Make it kinder. I'm saying this to my six-year-old: Your drawing is messy and the colours are wrong.
I can see you worked hard on this drawing. Shall we try mixing some new colours together next time?
Make this birthday message more grown-up for my manager: Happy bday!! Have a blast!!
Wishing you a very happy birthday. I hope you have a wonderful day and a great year ahead.

One past-tense paragraph, please, using linking words instead of day labels.

Monday: Bhavna's tower fell. "Mum-ma..." Her voice wobbled. Parul was on the phone and didn't look up. A minute later Bhavna was screaming on the floor.
Thursday: the tower fell again. "Mum-ma..." Parul heard the choke in it and came at once, holding her. Bhavna cried a little, then leaned in.
The next Monday: the same wobble. Parul put a hand on her back. Bhavna sniffed and started building again.

One Monday, Bhavna's tower fell. "Mum-ma..." she called, her voice wobbling, but Parul was on the phone and didn't look up. A minute later, Bhavna was screaming on the floor. On Thursday, the tower fell again. This time Parul heard the choke in her voice and came at once to hold her. Bhavna cried a little, then leaned in. The following Monday, the same wobble came, and Parul put a hand on her back. Bhavna sniffed and started building again.
Put this in the past tense: I wake up at six, make tea for Papa, and walk to the bus stop with Rohan. We talk about cricket until the bus comes.
I woke up at six, made tea for Papa, and walked to the bus stop with Rohan. We talked about cricket until the bus came.

Retell this in the first person, as Irawati's mother, Chandrika.

On parents' morning at the preschool, the block corner was busy. Usually Irawati built towers fast and knocked them over for fun. Today her mother, Chandrika, sat on a small chair right beside the mat. Irawati slowed down. She picked each block carefully, lined up the corners, and checked it wasn't wobbling. Twice she looked up to see if Amma was still watching. She was. When the tower was taller than her knees, Irawati sat back and pointed. 'Amma, see! Mine!' Chandrika clapped, and Irawati glowed.

On parents' morning at the preschool, the block corner was busy. Usually Irawati built towers fast and knocked them over for fun. Today I sat on a small chair right beside the mat. Irawati slowed down. She picked each block carefully, lined up the corners, and checked it wasn't wobbling. Twice she looked up to see if I was still watching. I was. When the tower was taller than her knees, Irawati sat back and pointed. 'Amma, see! Mine!' I clapped, and Irawati glowed.
Rewrite in the simple past: I have finished my homework, and my mother has checked it.
I finished my homework, and my mother checked it.

Put what people say here into reported speech.

Dolma had been sick with a cough and fever for three days. She was proud of drinking from a big-girl cup, but now she asked for her old baby bottle from the cupboard. She talked in a squeaky baby voice and crawled into Preeti's bed every night. Her aunt laughed, 'Such a big girl, acting like a baby!' Dolma hid her face. Preeti said gently, 'She's poorly. It's fine,' and filled the bottle with warm water. A week later, fever gone, Dolma pushed the bottle away herself. 'That's for babies.'

Dolma had been sick with a cough and fever for three days. She was proud of drinking from a big-girl cup, but now she asked for her old baby bottle from the cupboard. She talked in a squeaky baby voice and crawled into Preeti's bed every night. Her aunt laughed and said that she was such a big girl, acting like a baby. Dolma hid her face. Preeti said gently that Dolma was poorly and that it was fine, and filled the bottle with warm water. A week later, with the fever gone, Dolma pushed the bottle away herself and said that it was for babies.

Make this verse easier to follow.

But Sarama, of gentler mood,
With pitying eyes the mourner viewed,
Stole to her side and softly told
Glad tidings that her heart consoled,
Revealing with sweet voice and smile
The secret of the giant's guile.
She, one of those who night and day
Watching in turns by Sita lay,
Though Rakshas born felt pity's touch,
And loved the hapless lady much.

But Sarama, who was of a gentler mood, looked at the mourner with pitying eyes. She stole to her side and softly told her glad news that comforted her heart, revealing with a sweet voice and smile the secret of the giant's trickery. She was one of those who watched in turns by Sita night and day, and though she was born a Rakshas, she felt the touch of pity and loved the unhappy lady much.
Say this in modern English: Good morrow! I trust thou slept well.
Good morning! I hope you slept well.

Rewrite this in easier words.

At the lift of their Mumbai building, two-year-old Ramesh waved hard at the watchman. "Bye-bye!" he shouted, and the watchman waved back. Upstairs, a neighbour came to the door, beaming, and said, "Hello, Ramesh!" Ramesh pressed his face into his father's leg. Jatin did not push him. "He'll say hello when he's ready," he told her. Later Ramesh peeked out and gave a tiny wave.

At the lift of their Mumbai building, two-year-old Ramesh waved hard at the watchman. "Bye-bye!" he shouted, and the watchman waved back. Upstairs, a neighbour came to the door, smiling, and said, "Hello, Ramesh!" Ramesh hid his face against his father's leg. Jatin did not push him. "He'll say hello when he's ready," he told her. Later Ramesh peeked out and gave a tiny wave.

Make this a two-sentence version, shorter than the original.

Monday: Rajni cried and pointed at the fridge. "More!" Irfan gave her yogurt, and the crying stopped.
Wednesday: she cried again and pushed the yogurt away. "No!" Irfan checked the time. Past her nap. He took her to bed, and she slept.
Saturday: she cried, holding her foot. "Ow!" Irfan found a thorn from the garden in her heel, took it out gently and cleaned it.
Rajni cried three times in the week. On Monday yogurt stopped it, on Wednesday a nap was what she needed, and on Saturday Irfan found a thorn in her heel and gently took it out.
Change to the negative and keep it short: They found the keys.
They did not find the keys.
Make the subject plural and change the rest to match: The sparrow builds a nest in the window.
The sparrows build nests in the window.
I need an email subject line of five words or fewer for this: Meeting moved to Thursday because the manager is travelling.
Meeting moved to Thursday

Reduce this passage to three sentences.

This is what I saw in 10B on Tuesday. At lunch Lokesh pulled his friend Ritu aside and said something, and I heard the words "find out." Ritu then went over to the bench where Sonal sits and asked, loudly enough for the row to hear, "Do you like Lokesh?" Sonal looked at the tiffin box and said, "Why is he asking you?" By fourth period people were saying "Sonal likes Lokesh." I never heard Sonal say that. Sonal packed up her things and left early. Lokesh kept glancing at the door. I can't tell what either of them was thinking. I only saw that Sonal stopped talking to the bench group, and that Lokesh never got an answer from Sonal at all. - Nandini

Nandini saw Lokesh take his friend Ritu aside at lunch and say something with the words "find out" in it, after which Ritu went to Sonal's bench and loudly asked her whether she liked Lokesh. Sonal looked at her tiffin box and asked why he was asking her, but by fourth period people were saying that Sonal liked Lokesh, though Nandini never heard Sonal say that. Sonal packed up and left early, stopped talking to the bench group, and Lokesh never got an answer from her at all.

Rewrite this so a young child can follow it, with short sentences and easy words.

At Chaitanya's birthday party in the Bengaluru flat, the children sat on the carpet watching a cartoon. When the big storm came in the film and the little boat started to sink, Ramesh pulled his knees up and covered his ears. Chaitanya, the birthday boy, noticed. He shuffled over and held Ramesh's hand. "The boat's okay. I've seen it. Hold on." Ramesh held on. The boat bobbed back up. Ramesh laughed shakily. Later, when a younger cousin cried at the thunder in the film, Ramesh went and sat beside him. "Hold my hand. It gets better."

It was Chaitanya's birthday party in the Bengaluru flat. The children sat on the carpet and watched a cartoon. Then a big storm came in the film. The little boat began to sink. Ramesh pulled up his knees and covered his ears. Chaitanya, the birthday boy, saw this. He moved over and held Ramesh's hand. "The boat is okay. I have seen it. Hold on." Ramesh held on. The boat came back up. Ramesh laughed, and his laugh was a little shaky. Later, a younger cousin cried at the thunder in the film. Ramesh went and sat next to him. "Hold my hand," he said. "It gets better."

Retell this in the third person, as if it were about Gautam.

So I tipped the junk box from under the bed onto the floor: a flattened cardboard carton, twelve bottle caps, a bundle of ice-cream sticks, and a coil of old wire from a broken radio. I sat and looked.

So Gautam tipped the junk box from under the bed onto the floor: a flattened cardboard carton, twelve bottle caps, a bundle of ice-cream sticks, and a coil of old wire from a broken radio. He sat and looked.
Convert to the present tense: Lucas painted a picture of the sea.
Lucas paints a picture of the sea.
Reduce the number of words: At the present time, the shop is closed for lunch.
The shop is closed for lunch.
